items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He did a great deal, we did a lot of work together and had an awful lot of laughs.

ctx.x: He was wonderful you know, Gerry really came up with something when he came up with Chet, then after that when Chet left town, I graduated to Jack Sheldon and Jack Sheldon was quite something in those days, in the 50s still and the 60s. He did a great deal, we did a lot of work together and had an awful lot of laughs.
There is one story that I heard, that we might as well bring up now that when you did the score to, “The Sandpiper,” and you had him as a solo trumpet…

items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Well Johnny Mandel, I love him. We did “The Sandpiper” with “The Shadow of Your Smile,” and that’s still a great score.

ctx.x: What were some of your favorite soundtracks or writers for the movie thing?
Well Johnny Mandel, I love him. We did “The Sandpiper” with “The Shadow of Your Smile,” and that’s still a great score.
And you did a great thing on that, didn’t you?
